readme.html:
motion-tools-and-skills

Tools, agent skills, prompts and starters for making motion graphics with AI agents (Claude Code). The focus is code-rendered motion (Three.js + GSAP, HyperFrames, Remotion, Canvas, WebGL/WebGPU, p5.js) and agent-driven DCC tools (Blender, Unreal Engine, ComfyUI).

The first collection was gathered from ten open-source Opus 5.5 video projects on 6 October 2026, a second pass on 21 October added six more and refreshed three, a third on 22 October added five more, a fourth the same day added material from fifteen of twenty motion-skill repos, and a fifth on 4 November added the Anatomy isometric-explainer skill and a guide to React Bits (SOURCES.md). Everything copied here carries its upstream licence, and every folder has a NOTES.md that says what it does, when to use it, what it needs, and what was changed.

New here? Read docs/techniques.md first. It distils the shared method behind all of these projects into working rules for our stack.

What's inside

skills/ — Claude Code skills

Skill Makes
kinetic-reel Kinetic-typography reels and promos with three.js layers, a WebGL post pass and a synthesised beat-locked score
painted-animation Hand-painted watercolour cartoons, music and lyric videos (p5.brush); includes the best animation guide in the survey
motion-graphics-music-video Full music videos from a song: plan, generated characters on green, p5 motion graphics, SFX and VFX (Fal.ai key; VFX on macOS)
lemo-opuscar Short films in any of 51 film styles, made entirely in code, including Evidence Films from real data; turn a style into a house style
3d-product Product and object films in Blender (Cycles or Octane), from a patent, photos or CAD to a graded film, with a measured gate at every stage
video-production-skills Eleven editorial skills: evidence-linked script, shot plan, explainer-motion brief, voice and caption sync, cover, release QA
video-shotcraft Promo films in Remotion from 124 shot recipe cards with tuned components; the cards also work as timing specs for GSAP and HyperFrames (Remotion Company Licence needed for organisational use)
img2threejs One reference image → a code-only, rigged, animatable Three.js model, built in gated passes
lower-thirds Transparent lower thirds as ProRes 4444 / VP9 alpha, with alpha and title-safe checks
motion-design-principles Durations, stagger, overshoot and choreography decided before code (LottieFiles)
opus-visual-motion-engine HTML motion pieces with automated render QA (qa.mjs)
motion-designer Code films and overlays with a determinism gate, beat clock and music cut to whole bars
talking-head-b-roll Presenter graphics timed to the spoken words
claude-motion Taste rules with numbers, a frame-review loop, sound from one timeline.json
hyperframes-motion-reel Beat-locked reels in HyperFrames, with HyperFrames' rules and pitfalls
anatomy Isometric explainer figures: a technical idea drawn as a real, detailed machine with live parts, WebGL light and a readout; records to video

prompts/ — prompts and briefs

  • film-styles/: 51 film-style prompts (satellite briefing, archive light table, Swiss motion, data storytelling, isometric infographic, dark keynote, spy titles, glass product, ukiyo-e…) in one reusable 11-section schema.
  • starters/mg-styles-15/prompts/: 15 motion-design style prompts with the source of every film they made, a template for new styles and an AI-jury review rubric.
  • video-prompts/: 64 + 40 curated motion-design prompts and cases from two large collections of Opus 5.5 videos.

tools/ — render, check and finish

  • headless-render/: review sheets, frame strips, tracked crops and parallel rendering for any time-pure page; GPU probe for headless Chrome.
  • lemo-core/: parallel video render, reading-time check, loudness master with grain, procedural SFX, TTS with a Whisper check, three.js post and CRT passes.
  • song-analysis/: song → beat grid, downbeats, sections, per-instrument onsets from separated stems, loudness envelopes, and word-level lyric timing.
  • tidewater-asset-pipeline/: CC0 sound sourcing and −23 LUFS normalisation; Blender batch retargeting to GLB and decimation.
  • sync-check/: sound against picture in a rendered MP4 (off-beat hits, startling jumps).
  • mixamo-retarget/: human joints → animated Mixamo character GLB, in numpy, without Blender.
  • skills/3d-product/references/dsh-blender-modeling/: Blender modelling pitfalls, numeric gates, Blender 5.2 API breaks, three-view calibration, verifier checklist.
  • Plus beat detection, cut detection, green-screen keying, SFX mixing and a synth score inside the skills (listed in tools/README.md).

starters/ — templates to build on

  • tidewater-webgpu-fx/: FFT ocean, physical sky, caustics, lens flare, motion blur and a full post chain in raw WebGPU/WGSL, with headless capture.
  • pdoom-video-engine/: a three.js engine for audio-driven films with adaptive per-tile motion blur, true 4K from a 1080p layout and an HDR post chain.
  • mg-styles-15/: 15 motion-design films with full source, a renderAt(t) render harness and the mgaudio soundtrack toolkit.
  • papermotion/: a paper-cutout film engine with rigs, physics and simulation-driven sound, plus its skill.
  • dioramas/: cinematic 3D pages with volumetric light, reflections and an AgX post stack; image → 3D assets through fal (Nano Banana 2 → Meshy 7.1); deterministic video capture of any live-clock page (dioramas, Anatomy figures, React Bits components), with --scale and --clip.
  • Pointers to the kinetic-reel, painted-cartoon, web-intro and p5-overlay templates inside the skills.

docs/ — guides and research

  • techniques.md: the shared method, applied to our tools.
  • reference-only.md: useful material that could not be copied (no licence, or third-party content), with where to find it.
  • guides/lemo-opuscar/: directing and pipeline guides for code-made films, and how to make a style your own.
  • guides/: motion fundamentals (iart.ai), field rules for code films (Howseen), effect recipes, news-insert rules, motion tokens, Disney principles in frames.
  • guides/react-bits/: using React Bits backgrounds and text effects in films (loop export, frame-exact capture, picks, licence limits); nothing copied.
  • research/athemeroy/: a study of 1,000+ agent-made videos, with a production brief, production paths, workflow analysis and data.

Using a skill

Copy a skill folder into %USERPROFILE%\.claude\skills\ (Windows) or symlink it into ~/.claude/skills/ (macOS, Linux, WSL), then describe the video you want in Claude Code. Details in skills/README.md.

What stays out of git

Renders (*.mp4, *.mov, ProRes masters), Unreal caches (DerivedDataCache/, Intermediate/, Saved/, Binaries/), node_modules/, model weights, .env files and large media. See .gitignore.
